items.title: Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass
items.summary: Google Deepmind's new Gemini Decisions API evaluates up to 1,000 closed-ended questions in a single pass across text, images, audio, and video. Gemini Decision 1 returns results in 150 to 250 milliseconds at roughly five times lower cost than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, according to Google. The article Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: US corporate AI spending hits a new high in October, but growth slows to 1.65 percent
items.summary: According to the Ramp AI Index, US corporate AI spending rose just 1.65 percent in October 2026. One percent of companies still drive 80 percent of revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. Customer support is emerging as a new growth driver, but it may bring lower margins than the coding business that has fueled spending so far. The article US corporate AI spending hits a new high in October, but growth slows to 1.65 percent appeared first on The Decode

items.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks instead of years
items.summary: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code mathematically verified Signal's cryptographic core code in four weeks, a process that typically takes years. AI agents powered by Gemini Carbon wrote more than six million lines of proof code and flagged only about one percent for human review. items.title: Helsing built an AI system that prepares targets for weapons systems and says every decision will carry a human name
items.summary: Helsing has unveiled Clarity, an AI platform that uses agents to distill sensor data into target recommendations for weapons systems, all under human oversight and European control. But experience from the Iran war, Gaza, and a near-miss involving China shows that the speed of automation and data fusion create risks that are hard to contain. items.title: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead, cutting an AMD chip switch from months to three days
items.summary: Anthropic claims it used AI itself to breach Nvidia's CUDA moat. The company's in-house model Mythos reportedly ported Claude to AMD GPUs in just three days, with almost no human intervention. Anthropic now runs Claude on four chip families and aims to cut costs and reduce vendor dependencies. The article Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia's CUDA lead, cutting an AMD chip switch from months to three days appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: US data brokers are selling half a billion dollars in RL training environments to Chinese AI labs
items.summary: US data brokers like Mercor, Surge AI, and AfterQuery are selling roughly half a billion dollars' worth of AI training data to Chinese labs, according to a ChinaTalk investigation. That includes the same RL environments previously built for OpenAI or Anthropic. At least nine firms are involved, and export controls barely apply. items.title: DeepL wants real-time translation to finally capture sarcasm and mood shifts
items.summary: DeepL Voice's real-time translations are about to sound a lot more natural. The company's new Aure model carries over tone, emotion, emphasis, and speaking pace from the original speaker's voice into the target language. The article DeepL wants real-time translation to finally capture sarcasm and mood shifts appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Grok-built apps exposed patient data, plaintext passwords, and SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline
items.summary: Security firm Claroc found more than 35,000 Grok-built apps open to anyone without login, including patient data and confidential SpaceXSI documents. The cause: "Anyone with the link" was preselected as the default access setting. SpaceXSI took only its own 24 employee apps offline. The rest remain accessible. The article Grok-built apps exposed patient data, plaintext passwords, and SpaceXSI's own sales pipeline appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
items.summary: OpenAI grew its quarterly revenue 50 percent to $10 billion but is still burning more cash than it brings in. Adjusted operating losses climbed to $10.9 billion, while rival Anthropic operates far more efficiently on $17 billion in revenue. To close the gap, OpenAI is now fueling a price war for enterprise customers. items.title: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
items.summary: England's higher education regulator, the Office for Students, says AI has made it "nearly impossible" to fairly assess student coursework. An investigation found that students are having ChatGPT write entire papers undetected, without being able to recall basic content afterward.
